02 Scenarios

What could go wrong.

01 / Natural disasterM7+

Earthquake

A major quake on the Cascadia or Georgia Strait faults. Bridges and tunnels are closed for inspection within minutes. The family is split between home, school, and office, and no one can get to anyone else.

  • 0–1 hrCell networks saturate. Calls fail; texts queue. Power is out across the region.
  • 1–24 hrWater pressure drops or stops. Fuel stations close. Roads become one-way out.
  • Day 2+Stores are empty. Emergency services triage by severity, not by address. You are on your own for a week or more.
02 / InfrastructureGrid

Attack on infrastructure

An automated attack on utilities and telecoms. Nothing is physically damaged, and that is the problem: there is no visible event, no timeline, and no one who can say when it ends.

  • 0–1 hrPower, internet, and mobile data fail together. Payment terminals, ATMs, and fuel pumps stop.
  • 1–24 hrTraffic signals and transit go dark. Water treatment runs on backup. Building access systems lock or fail open.
  • Day 2+Cash runs out. Refrigeration fails. Restoration is measured in days to weeks with no public estimate.
03 / SecurityLockdown

Terrorist attack

A coordinated attack downtown. The city core is sealed. If a family member works, studies, or is in transit there, they are inside the cordon with no way out and no way to reach you.

  • 0–1 hrLockdown. Transit halts, bridges close, cell networks are overloaded by everyone calling at once.
  • 1–24 hrCordons expand. Movement is restricted. Information is fragmented and mostly wrong.
  • Day 2+Secondary threats keep areas closed. Reuniting the family depends entirely on a plan made in advance.

In each case the first failure is the same: communication, then movement, then supply. The system we build covers all three.
